But, Socinus, the salvation and justification of the Gentiles is not the norm and exemplary cause of the salvation of believers, nor is the salvation of Peter and the faithful the main question, but the salvation of the Gentiles. According to Socinus' mind, Peter ought to have said: The law is not to be laid on the neck of the Gentiles or the disciples, because we too will be saved in the same way as they. What need of argument is there here? Indeed, what does this speech do for its own purpose, which is perverted by such reasoning rather than helped by it? Next, the contrast between the yoke and the grace of Jesus Christ is too manifest. The Fathers did not bear the yoke. How then were they justified, when there is no release without bearing and satisfaction? Namely, the grace of Jesus Christ, who took up the yoke of the curse and the handwriting and bore it on the cross, and so, having borne it away, acquired for us complete liberty. Who does not see that the adversative particle ἀλλὰ [but] answers the negation immediately before it? To such a reader nothing can be coloured. Let the fraudulent distortion therefore depart. Indeed, as in Adam all die, so in Christ all are made alive, 1 Cor. 15:22. And there is no salvation in anyone else outside Christ, Acts 4:12, which cannot be restricted to the New Testament, because the Apostle there urges the necessity of obtaining salvation through Christ. Next, Christ is said in plain words to have redeemed τὰς ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ παραβάσεις [the transgressions under the first covenant], those sins which were under the first covenant, Heb. 9:15. This cannot be twisted to mean sins of the same kind, namely that Christ by his blood redeemed sins of such a kind as could not be expiated by legal sacrifices. This clashes with the Apostle's purpose, which is to show that the sacrifice of Christ was necessary. For if in the Old Testament sins were expiated by any sacrifice, there would have been no need for a sacrifice in the New Testament. But the Apostle meant that sins were not expiated in the Old Testament; therefore there was need of a sacrifice in the New Testament. Otherwise the Fathers would have perished. Hence in v. 22 he says: without shedding of blood there is no remission. This could easily be refuted if the Fathers were redeemed without shedding of blood. Indeed, the blood of goats and bulls intervened. But the Apostle denies that this could cleanse the conscience, and from this he concludes that redemption through Christ was necessary. Indeed, in v. 23 he says it was necessary that the heavens be purified by some better sacrifice. But the heavens are sanctified not on their own account but on ours. Christ had indeed not yet been made man in the Old Testament. Yet the efficacy of Christ's death could be carried back. For the merit of Christ is the moral cause of justification, and the nature of such a cause is that it can have force even when it is not yet actually in existence; it is, as they say in the Schools, to have being known. Of this there are very many examples in life. For there could be no dealings among men if promises had no force until after they were fulfilled.

units.la: CAPUT XI. Conciliaris sententia Jacobi discutitur.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI. The conciliar opinion of James is examined.

units.la: Breviarium.
units.tr: Summary.

units.la: Iacobi Conciliaris sententia exponitur. Silentium multitudinis non fuisse argumentum praesidentia Petri. Deum per miracula hodie non attestari veritati. Quae ratio sit, disquiritur. Iacobus quis fuerit? Quomodo frater Christi? An Συμεὼν & Σίμων nomina distincta? Cur Simoni inditum nomen Petri? Toletus, Baronius censentur. Iustini Martyris observatio probata. Ἐμπεπλεν ἐξ ἰθνῶν. Populum sumere suo nomini. Scripturarum authoritas. Prophetia Amos illustratur. Abarbanel notatur. סכת דוד. Σκηνὴ Δαυΐδ Christus est. Locus 2. Sam. VII. 11. Καταναμμένα. הרסות Amos & Iacobus conciliantur. LXX. Interpretes non sunt authentici. Cur praecipuè Edom à reliquiis Israelis haereditandus? Locus Psal. LX, 10. 11. expositus. Invocare nomen super aliquo. Verba Iacobi: Deo ab aeterno omnia sua opera sunt nota, explicantur & à Socini corruptelis vindicantur. cantur. Παρενοχλεῖν. Inquiritur in genuinum sensum versus XXI. Chrysostomus, Cornelius à Lapide, Grotius, Curcellæus, Stephanus Aretius improbantur. Beza explicatio adoptatur. Lectionis Legis in Synagogis antiquitas.
units.tr: The conciliar opinion of James is set out. The silence of the multitude was not an argument for Peter's presidency. God does not today attest the truth through miracles. The reason for this is inquired into. Who was James? How was he the brother of Christ? Are Συμεὼν and Σίμων distinct names? Why was the name of Peter given to Simon? Toletus and Baronius are considered. The observation of Justin Martyr is approved. Ἐμπεπλεν ἐξ ἰθνῶν [from the Gentiles]. The taking of a people for his name. The authority of the Scriptures. The prophecy of Amos is illustrated. Abarbanel is noted. סכת דוד [sukkat David]. Σκηνὴ Δαυΐδ [the tabernacle of David] is Christ. The passage 2 Sam. 7:11 is considered. Καταναμμένα [ruined places]. הרסות [ruins]. Amos and James are reconciled. The Septuagint translators are not authentic. Why is Edom especially to inherit from the remnant of Israel? Psalm 60:10, 11 is expounded. To invoke a name over someone. The words of James: all his works are known to God from eternity are explained and vindicated from the corruptions of Socinus. cantur. Παρενοχλεῖν [to trouble]. An inquiry is made into the genuine sense of verse 21. Chrysostom, Cornelius à Lapide, Grotius, Curcellaeus and Stephanus Aretius are rejected. The explanation of Beza is adopted. The antiquity of the reading of the Law in the synagogues.

units.la: GRavissimam Petri Orationem, quâ Gentiles hactenus conversos asseruit in communionem gratiæ Iesu Christi, & jugum ἀδάσκητον illorum cervici intentatum depulit, excepit tum Barnabæ & Pauli, tum Jacobi sermo. Commemorat Lucas continuis versibus decem, qui sequuntur.
units.tr: The very weighty speech of Peter, by which he asserted that the Gentiles converted so far were admitted into fellowship with the grace of Jesus Christ, and removed the yoke of unlawful (?) bondage laid on their necks, was followed by the speech of Barnabas and Paul, and then of James. Luke relates in the ten verses that follow:

units.la: 12. Ἐσίγησε δὲ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος, ἠκουον Βαρνάβα καὶ Παύλου ἐξηγουμένων, ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι δι' αὐτῶν.
units.tr: 12. And all the multitude kept silence, and listened to Barnabas and Paul relating what signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them. [Ἐσίγησε δὲ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος, ἠκουον Βαρνάβα καὶ Παύλου ἐξηγουμένων, ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι δι' αὐτῶν.]

units.la: 13. Μετὰ δὲ τὸ σιγῆσαι αὐτούς, ἀπεκρίθη Ἰάκωβος, λέγων. Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἀκούσατέ μου.
units.tr: 13. And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying: Men and brethren, hearken unto me. [Μετὰ δὲ τὸ σιγῆσαι αὐτούς, ἀπεκρίθη Ἰάκωβος, λέγων. Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἀκούσατέ μου.]

units.la: 14. Συμεὼν ἐξηγήσατο, καθὼς πρῶτον ὁ Θεὸς ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν λαὸν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
units.tr: 14. Simeon has declared how God first visited to take from the Gentiles a people for his name. [Συμεὼν ἐξηγήσατο, καθὼς πρῶτον ὁ Θεὸς ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν λαὸν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.]

units.la: 15. Καὶ τούτῳ συμφωνοῦσι οἱ λόγοι τῶν προφητῶν, καθὼς γέγραπται.
units.tr: 15. And to this agree the words of the prophets, as it is written: [Καὶ τούτῳ συμφωνοῦσι οἱ λόγοι τῶν προφητῶν, καθὼς γέγραπται.]

units.la: 16. Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναστρέψω, καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσω τὴν σκηνὴν Δαβὶδ τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν, καὶ τὰ κατεσκαμμένα αὐτῆς ἀνοικοδομήσω, καὶ ἀνορθώσω αὐτήν.
units.tr: 16. After this I will return and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down, and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: [Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναστρέψω, καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσω τὴν σκηνὴν Δαβὶδ τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν, καὶ τὰ κατεσκαμμένα αὐτῆς ἀνοικοδομήσω, καὶ ἀνορθώσω αὐτήν.]

units.la: 17. Ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν Κύριον, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, ἐφ' οὓς ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπ' αὐτούς. Λέγει Κύριος, ὁ ποιῶν ταῦτα πάντα.
units.tr: 17. That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things. [Ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν Κύριον, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, ἐφ' οὓς ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπ' αὐτούς. Λέγει Κύριος, ὁ ποιῶν ταῦτα πάντα.]

units.la: 12. Tacuit autem tota multitudo, & audiebant Paulum & Barnabam narrantes, quaecunque Deus edidisset signa & miracula inter Gentes per ipsos.
units.tr: 12. Then all the multitude kept silence, and they heard Paul and Barnabas declaring what God had done among the Gentiles by them.

units.la: 13. Et postquam conticuissent, respondit Iacobus, dicens: Viri Fratres, audite me:
units.tr: 13. And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying: Men, brethren, hear me.

units.la: 14. Symeon narravit, quemadmodum Deus primum visitaverit, ut sumeret ex Gentibus populum in nomine suo.
units.tr: 14. Simeon has declared how God first visited the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.

units.la: 15. Et huic consonant verba Prophetarum, sicut scriptum est:
units.tr: 15. And to this agree the words of the prophets, as it is written:

units.la: 16. Posthaec revertar & reaedificabo tabernaculum David, quod collapsum est & diruta eius instaurabo, & erigam illud.
units.tr: 16. After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen; and I will build up the ruins thereof, and I will set it up again:

units.la: 17. Ut requirant, qui reliqui sunt homines Dominum, & omnes gentes, super quas invocatum est nomen meum; dicit Dominus, qui facit haec omnia.
units.tr: 17. That the rest of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things.

units.la: 18. Γνωσὸς
units.tr: 18. Known [Γνωσὸς]

units.la: 18. Γνωσὸν ἀπ' αἰῶνός ἐστι τῷ Θεῷ πάντα τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ.
units.tr: 18. Known from the beginning to God are all his works. [Γνωσὸν ἀπ' αἰῶνός ἐστι τῷ Θεῷ πάντα τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ.]

units.la: 19. Διὸ ἐγὼ κρίνω, μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν Θεόν.
units.tr: 19. Wherefore I judge that we should not trouble those of the Gentiles who turn to God, [Διὸ ἐγὼ κρίνω, μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν Θεόν.]

units.la: 20. Ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι αὐτοῖς τοῦ ἀπέχεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων, καὶ τῆς πορνείας καὶ τοῦ πνικτοῦ, καὶ τοῦ αἵματος.
units.tr: 20. But that we write to them that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood. [Ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι αὐτοῖς τοῦ ἀπέχεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων, καὶ τῆς πορνείας καὶ τοῦ πνικτοῦ, καὶ τοῦ αἵματος.]

units.la: 21. Μωϋσῆς γὰρ ἐκ γενεῶν ἀρχαίων κατὰ πόλιν τοὺς κηρύσσοντας αὐτὸν ἔχει, ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς κατὰ πᾶν Σάββατον ἀναγινωσκόμενος.
units.tr: 21. For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day. [Μωϋσῆς γὰρ ἐκ γενεῶν ἀρχαίων κατὰ πόλιν τοὺς κηρύσσοντας αὐτὸν ἔχει, ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς κατὰ πᾶν Σάββατον ἀναγινωσκόμενος.]

units.la: 18. Nota à Seculo sunt Deo omnia hæc opera sua.
units.tr: 18. Known from the world are all these works of his to God.

units.la: 19. Quapropter ego censeo, non obturbandum esse illis, qui ex gentibus convertuntur ad Deum.
units.tr: 19. Wherefore I judge that those who are converted to God from among the Gentiles should not be troubled.

units.la: 20. Sed scribendum ad eos, ut abstineant se ab inquinamentis simulacrorum & fornicatione, & suffocato & sanguine.
units.tr: 20. But that they should be written to, to abstain from the pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from what is strangled, and from blood.

units.la: 21. Moses enim ab antiquis in singulis civitatibus habet qui ipsum prædicent in Synagogis, ubi per omne Sabbatum legitur.
units.tr: 21. For Moses from ancient generations has in every city those who preach him, being read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.

units.la: VERSUS XII. TACUIT AUTEM TOTA MULTITUDO)
units.tr: VERSE XII. AND THE WHOLE MULTITUDE KEPT SILENCE.

units.la: Oratione Petri nonnihil composita, quæ à principio turbare cœperat. Nempe ejusmodi erant argumenta Petri, ut adversariis, quod reponerent, non esset in promptu. Cornelius à Lapide hoc multitudinis silentium trahit in argumentum præsidentiæ Petri. Sue silentio, inquit, reverens Petrum, & ejus dicta approbans, ipsius sententia & definitioni acquievit. Scilicet Concilio illi interfuerint Pontifícii, qui in Reverentia Petri, tanquam summi Pontificis ita stupuerunt, ut in caudices & saxa abirent. Non fuit, Corneli, fictitia præsidentia Petri hujus silentii ratio, sed claritas argumentorum, quibus nemo obmutire poterat. Hæc vis veritatis est, non authoritatis, ad ἐχέμυθίαν redigere. Cæterum multitudinis meminit Lucas. Quod vel intelligi potest de toto Synodi corpore, vel de Ecclesia etiam Hierosolymitana, quæ non tantum per delectos ad Concilium, & consultationem institutam, sed tota adfuisse videtur.
units.tr: After Peter's speech, which had at first begun to stir them up, had been somewhat settled. Indeed, Peter's arguments were of such a kind that his opponents had nothing ready to answer. Cornelius à Lapide draws this silence of the multitude into an argument for Peter's presidency: "By their silence," he says, "they showed reverence for Peter, approved his words, and acquiesced in his opinion and decision." So, of course, the Papists who were present at that council were so amazed at Peter's reverence, as though he were the supreme Pontiff, that they turned into stumps and stones. Corneli, the cause of this silence was not a fictitious presidency of Peter but the clarity of the arguments, against which no one could be silent. This is the force of truth, not of authority, which reduces to silence (ἐχέμυθίαν). Moreover, Luke mentions the multitude. This can be understood either of the whole body of the Synod, or of the Church of Jerusalem also, which seems to have been present not only through those chosen for the Council and the consultation that was set up, but entire.

units.la: ET AUDIERUNT BARNABAM ET PAULUM)
units.tr: AND THEY HEARD BARNABAS AND PAUL)

units.la: Hi secundo loco sententiam dicunt, & approbant summam eorum, quæ dixerat Petrus, sed alia ratione utuntur, quæ sequitur.
units.tr: These men speak second and approve the substance of what Peter had said, but they use a different line of argument, which follows.

units.la: NARRANTES, QUÆCUNQUE DEUS EDIDISSET SIGNA INTER GENTES)
units.tr: Declaring what signs God had wrought among the Gentiles)

units.la: Argumento non minus evidenti comprobant. Gentiles ad communionem gratiæ sine circumcisione, sola dignatione Dei pertigisse. Quasi dicerent: Si ex eo testimonio, quod Deus Gentibus incircumcisis dedit per Petrum in conversione Cornelii, statuitis, non esse Gentibus Mosis legem imperandam, quid de eo facietis, quod Deus eisdem gentibus per miracula nostra inter illas patrata tam clare attestatus est? Ac deinde narrarunt miracula in Cypro, Pisidia, Lycaonia, &c. quae superioribus capitibus commemorantur. Apparet hinc, testimonium per miracula Deum perhiberi, si quando novandus est Ecclesiae status, & infideles ad illam adducendi. Nullo igitur jure a Reformatoribus nostris, quorum Sacro-Sancta nobis memoria est, Pontificii miracula postularunt. Equidem non novarunt Ecclesiae statum, sed renovarunt ad veterem normam, ἀπὸ ἐπιδοξίων τοῖς ἁγίοις πίστεως Jud. v.3. Neque res iis fuit cum Gentilibus, vel ejusmodi aliis, apud quos nomen Christi nondum nominatum, sed cum iis, qui Christo nomen suum Sacramento dederunt. Alia & maxime disparata ratio fuit Christi & Apostolorum, & Ecclesiae libertate uti incipientis. Nam eo tempore & Ecclesiae status novandus fuit, & antiquanda vetus falsa Gentilium doctrina, hoc est, Ecclesiae, quae hactenus in forma servientis erat, status commutandus fuit liberioris, & Gentiles hactenus repudiati, in viis suis euntes ab idololatrico cultu ad Christum convertendi. Hic Deo placuit, Gentibus & Judaeis per Evangelii signacula μαρτυρήσαι, quo Christus agnosceretur, & a Gentibus & a Judaeis, & major Mose, cujus decreta antiquanda, & Conciliator Israelis, & Ablator ac Sanator morborum nostrorum, & mortis Triumphator, & Sanator animae per doctrinam, atque adeo is, in quo promissiones Dei haberent τὸ ναὶ ἐν τῷ Ἀμήν. Quae omnia, quia a Reformatoribus nostris comprobari non debuerunt, quippe claris Scripturis jam demonstrata, & miraculis Christi & Apostolorum corroborata, & a toto Christianismo saltem professione recepta; non necesse habuerunt miraculorum accessione sibi fidem conciliare. Imo cum tam evidentibus documentis res contestata fuerit, Deum tentasset, quisquis a miraculis praesidium addidisset vel experiisset. Verissime & sapientissime, & plane ex mente nostra, & ex necessitate Ecclesiae Augustinus contra Faustum lib.13.cap.5. Unde huc existis, unde confidistis? Scripturas tanta authoritate firmatas commendatasque respuistis, miracula non facitis: quae si faceretis, etiam ipsa in vobis caveremus per instrumentem nos Dominum & dicentem: Exurgent multi Pseudochristi & Pseudoprophetae, & facient signa & prodigia multa, ut fallant, si fieri potest, etiam electos. Ecce praedixi vobis. Usque adeo nihil credi voluit adversus confirmatam Scripturarum authoritatem, quæ fidem suadere ipsis probat, quæ per temporum successiones hæc impleri & effici ostendit, quæ tanto antequam fierent, prænunciavit.
units.tr: They confirm it by an argument no less clear. The Gentiles attained to fellowship in grace without circumcision, by the sheer favour of God. It is as if they said: If from the testimony that God gave to the uncircumcised Gentiles through Peter at the conversion of Cornelius you conclude that the law of Moses is not to be imposed on the Gentiles, what will you make of the fact that God bore equally clear witness to those same Gentiles through the miracles we have performed among them? Then they recounted the miracles in Cyprus, Pisidia, Lycaonia, and so on, which are mentioned in the earlier chapters. It appears from this that God bears witness through miracles whenever the state of the Church is to be renewed and unbelievers are to be brought into it. Therefore our Reformers, whose memory is most sacred to us, had no right to demand miracles from the Papists. Indeed they did not change the state of the Church but restored it to the old norm, ἀπὸ ἐπιδοξίων τοῖς ἁγίοις πίστεως (Jude 3). Nor did they have to do with Gentiles or others of that kind, among whom the name of Christ had not yet been named, but with those who had given their name to Christ in the sacrament. The situation of Christ and the Apostles was different and altogether dissimilar, for they were beginning to use the freedom of the Church. For at that time the state of the Church had to be renewed, the ancient false doctrine of the Gentiles had to be overturned, that is, the state of the Church, which had hitherto been in the form of a servant, had to be changed into a freer one, and the Gentiles, hitherto rejected, had to be converted from idolatrous worship to Christ as they went on their way. Here God was pleased to bear witness (μαρτυρήσαι) to Gentiles and Jews by the signs of the Gospel, so that Christ might be acknowledged both by Gentiles and by Jews as greater than Moses, whose decrees were to be set aside, as the reconciler of Israel, the remover and healer of our diseases, the conqueror of death, and the healer of the soul through doctrine; and so he is the one in whom the promises of God have τὸ ναὶ ἐν τῷ Ἀμήν (2 Cor. 1:20). Since our Reformers were not obliged to confirm all these things, which had already been demonstrated by clear Scriptures, confirmed by the miracles of Christ and the Apostles, and received by the whole of Christianity at least in profession, they had no need to win faith for themselves by the addition of miracles. Indeed, when the matter had been attested by such evident proofs, whoever had added or sought the support of miracles would have tempted God. Most truly and wisely, and entirely in accordance with our mind and the needs of the Church, Augustine says against Faustus, book 13, chapter 5: Whence have you come, and on what do you rely? You have rejected Scriptures confirmed and commended by such great authority, and you do not work miracles. Even if you did work them, we would still be on guard against them in you, through the Lord who warned us and said: Many false Christs and false prophets will arise, and will show great signs and wonders, so as to deceive, if it were possible, even the elect. Behold, I have told you beforehand. So far was it desired that nothing be believed against the confirmed authority of the Scriptures, which proves that faith is to be persuaded to them, which shows that these things are fulfilled and accomplished through the successions of times, which foretold them so long before they came to pass.

units.la: Versus XIII. ET POSTQUAM CONTICUISSENT, RESPONDIT JACOBUS)
units.tr: Verse 13. AND AFTER THEY HAD BEEN SILENT, JAMES ANSWERED)

units.la: Jacobus, Filius Alphæi, in catalogo Apostolorum ordine nonus, Matth. cap. X. 3. Vocatur Frater Domini, Gal. I. 19. Photius dicit, Fratrem Domini vocari ob similitudinem cum Christo. Parum probabile. Nam etiam alii dicuntur Fratres Christi, Joh. XX. 17. Quos omnes similes Christo fuisse nemo dixerit. Frater igitur Christi vocatur, quia consanguineus, quippe natus ex Matertera Christi, Alphæo nupta. De vita, morte & constantia hujus Apostoli videsis Eusebium Hist. Eccles. II. 23. & Josephum Antiq. XX. 16. Respondere dicitur usitato Hebraismo etiam non interrogatus, qui sermonem inchoat, ut notum est. Cæterum jam supra observavimus & probavimus, Jacobi sententiam fuisse definitivam, ut Præsidis. Quamobrem nolumus hic per eandem lineam serram reciprocare.
units.tr: James, son of Alphaeus, ninth in the catalogue of the Apostles, Matt. 10:3, is called the brother of the Lord, Gal. 1:19. Photius says that he is called the brother of the Lord because of his likeness to Christ. This is not very probable, for others too are called brethren of Christ, John 20:17, and no one would say that all of them were like Christ. Therefore he is called the brother of Christ because he was a kinsman, being born of Christ's aunt, who was married to Alphaeus. For the life, death and constancy of this Apostle, see Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History II.23, and Josephus, Antiquities XX.16. He is said to answer, by the customary Hebraism, even though he was not asked, which is the way of beginning a speech, as is well known. Moreover, we have already observed and shown above that James's opinion was definitive, as that of the president. Wherefore we do not wish to saw back and forth along the same line here.

units.la: DICENS) Summa dictorum: Congruere sententiam Petri cum scriptis Prophetarum & Divinis oraculis, ideoque recipiendam, & pauculis additis de necessaria à quibusdam abstinentia, in eam decretum formandum: id quod re ipsa facit.
units.tr: SAYING) The sum of his words: Peter's opinion agrees with the writings of the Prophets and the divine oracles, and therefore is to be received; and with a few additions concerning a necessary abstinence from certain things, a decree is to be formed upon it. This is what he in fact does.

units.la: Versus XIV. SIMON NARRAVIT) Συμεὼν. Alibi Σίμων vocatur.
units.tr: Verse 14. SIMON HAS RELATED) Συμεὼν. Elsewhere he is called Σίμων.

units.la: Sunt, quibus videatur esse duo distincta nomina. Rectius divinat Laurentius Valla, quem sequuntur Erasmus, Beza, Cornelius à Lapide, nihil interesse inter Simon & Simeon: nisi quod Simeon Hebraicè dicatur, Græcè inflexa voce Simon. Nempe Hebraicè dicunt שִׁמְעוֹן per Scheva quiescens, quod Græci faciunt mobile. Nisi malimus dicere, Gutturalem y modò plane non exprimi, modò habere correspondentem vocalem E. Notum enim, literas Gutturales in aliis linguis non habere consonas, quæ respondeant, sed ab illis liberè assumi vocalem, vel plane omitti. Toletus in Joh. 1. annotat. 64. deducit à Rad. שמן impinguavit, ut Simon idem sit quod pinguis, vel impinguatus oleo, & gratia Spiritus S. Nimis jejune. Est enim Simeon שמעון audiens, obediens. Christus μετονομάζει Joh. I. 43. & vocat Simeonem Cephām, Petrum. Rationem reddit Baronius, nempe primatum Petri, seu omnipotentiam Romani Pontificis. Ita ubique in themate suo primario stupet. Alii sunt, qui aliud nihil Christum spectâsse contendant, nisi ut hoc novo cognomine Simeonem, Andreæ Fratrem, discerneret à Simone Cananite, sive Zelota. Nimis istud dilutum, & alta Christi sapientia indignum. Justinus Martyr in Tryphone erudite observat, Christum cum Ecclesiæ suæ jaciebat fundamenta, inter alia numero infinita argumenta, quibus probavit, eundem se esse illum Deum, quem Prophetæ & Patriarchæ adoraverant, istud etiam adhibuisse, quòd discipulorum suorum nonnullis nova nomina imposuit, sicut olim in Abrahamo, Sara & Jacobo erat factum. Nimirum dominantis esse, & illius, qui aliquem in sua potestate habeat, novum illi nomen imponere. Deinde haud dubie novo nomine Christus Petrum sui officii voluit monere, sicut sapienter olim Stoici censuerunt, nomina esse fontes, unde in hac vita officia manant. Admonere igitur Christus Simonem voluit, ut constans sit in professione Christi, & si alibi fortasse mollis, hic ut petra.
units.tr: Some think these are two distinct names. Laurentius Valla divines more correctly, and he is followed by Erasmus, Beza, and Cornelius à Lapide, that there is no difference between Simon and Simeon, except that Simeon is the Hebrew form and Simon the Greek form with an inflected ending. For in Hebrew they write שִׁמְעוֹן (Shimon) with a quiescent sheva, which the Greeks render as a movable vowel. Unless we prefer to say that the guttural y is now not expressed at all, and now has a corresponding vowel E. For it is known that the guttural letters in other languages have no matching consonants, but that a vowel is freely assumed by them or altogether omitted. Toletus, on John 1, note 64, derives it from the root שמן (shamen), "he made fat," so that Simon means the same as fat, or anointed with oil, and by the grace of the Holy Spirit. This is too thin. For Simeon (שמעון) means hearing, obeying. Christ changes his name, John 1:43, and calls Simeon Cephas (Cephām), that is, Peter. Baronius gives the reason: namely the primacy of Peter, or the omnipotence of the Roman Pontiff. Thus he everywhere marvels at his own chief theme. There are others who contend that Christ aimed at nothing else than to distinguish Simeon, the brother of Andrew, by this new surname from Simon the Canaanite, or the Zealot. That is too watery, and unworthy of the high wisdom of Christ. Justin Martyr, in the Dialogue with Trypho, learnedly observes that Christ, when laying the foundations of his Church, used among his countless arguments by which he proved that he was the same God whom the Prophets and Patriarchs had worshipped, also this one: that he gave new names to some of his disciples, just as had once been done with Abraham, Sarah and Jacob. Indeed it belongs to one who rules, and who has someone under his power, to impose a new name on him. Then, undoubtedly, by the new name Christ wished to remind Peter of his office, just as the Stoics wisely held that names are the sources from which duties flow in this life. Christ therefore wished to admonish Simon to be steadfast in the confession of Christ, and, if elsewhere perhaps soft, here to be like a rock.

units.la: QUEMADMODUM DEUS PRIMUM VISITAVERIT UT SUMERET EX GENTIBUS) Ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν. Videtur esse metathesis vocum Hebraeis usitata, in hunc ordinem resolvenda: Deus visitavit ex Gentibus, id est, gentes, ut ex iis sumat &c. Absque hac metathesi est, erit obscura Jacobi oratio. S. Cyprianus lib. II. contra Judaeos cap.7. pro visitavit habet prospexit, alii providit, alii cogitavit. Quae eodem redeunt. Sic Lucas cap.I. vers. 68. Benedictus Dominus Deus Israëlis ὅτι ἐπεσκέψατο καὶ ἐποίησε λύτρωσιν τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ. Sumere populum notat actum gratuitum misericordiae Dei, sibi secernentis populum ex iis, qui sedebant in tenebris & umbra mortis. Iccirco Lucas illam ἐπισκοπὴν deputat τοῖς ἀπλάγχνοις ἐλέους τῆς Θεοῦ. Cap.I. 78,79.
units.tr: HOW GOD FIRST VISITED TO TAKE FROM THE GENTILES) Ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν. This seems to be a metathesis of words, common in Hebrew, to be resolved into this order: God visited from among the Gentiles, that is, visited the Gentiles, so as to take from them, etc. Without this metathesis James's speech would be obscure. S. Cyprian, book II against the Jews, chapter 7, has "looked upon" for "visited," others "provided," others "thought of," which come to the same thing. So Luke 1:68: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, because he has visited and wrought redemption for his people" (ὅτι ἐπεσκέψατο καὶ ἐποίησε λύτρωσιν τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ). To take a people denotes the free act of God's mercy, separating for himself a people from those who sat in darkness and the shadow of death. Hence Luke ascribes that visitation (ἐπισκοπὴν) to the tender mercy of God (τοῖς σπλάγχνοις ἐλέους τοῦ Θεοῦ), Luke 1:78-79.

units.la: POPULUM) Hactenus Deus unum & alterum ex gentibus visitaverat, & ad Judaismum, suscepti ejus ritibus, traduxerat. Sed in universum gentes fuere Io-Ammah, & Io-Ruhamah. Nunc cum visitat Deus ex alto, fiunt populus Dei, quem Deus commiseratione prosequitur. Confer Jes.XLIII.1.3.4.6.7. Psal.C.3.
units.tr: THE PEOPLE) Until now God had visited one or another from among the Gentiles and had brought them over to Judaism, taking up its rites. But in general the Gentiles were Lo-ammi and Lo-ruhamah. Now, when God visits from on high, they become the people of God, whom God follows with compassion. Compare Isaiah 43:1, 3, 4, 6, 7; Psalm 100:3.

units.la: NOMINI SUO) τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ. Beza, idem quod שְׁמִי. Est autem ἀντιφρασικῶς dictum Nomini suo, id est sibi. Aut huc respexit Jacobus, quòd Sancti à Christo Christiani cognominentur. Haec posterior explicatio magis placet, recepta etiam Glossæ, Hugoni, Vatablo. Hebraismus est, quo populum Deus dicitur sumere nomini suo, id est, qui de nomine suo Ecclesia Dei vocetur, & propter illam adoptionem Deum glorificet, & ei in decoro Sanctitatis serviat. Apud Hebraeos קרא בשם יהוה vocari de nomine Dei. Confer Genes. IV. 26.
units.tr: TO HIS NAME) [τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ] Beza renders this as the equivalent of [שְׁמִי] "my name." It is said antiphrastically, "to his name," that is, "to himself." Or James may have had in mind that the saints are called Christians from Christ. This second explanation pleases me more, and it is also accepted by the Gloss, Hugo and Vatablus. It is a Hebraism by which the people are said to be taken for God's name, that is, the people who are called the Church of God from his name, who through that adoption glorify God and serve him in the splendour of holiness. Among the Hebrews, [קרא בשם יהוה] means "to be called by the name of the Lord." Compare Genesis 4:26.

units.la: Versus XV. ET HUIC CONSONANT VERBA PROPHETARUM) Provocat ad tempus promissionis, Prophetiae, visionis & exspectationis. Sic moris est Apostolis ad Mosen & Prophetas dictorum suorum veritatem referre. Et ut authoritatem ac potentiam verbi Dei aestimare discamus, Jacobus illam proponit evidentibus testimoniis Dei, a donato gentibus Spiritu Dei, a purificatione cordis, a fide, a gratia Jesu Christi, a signis & miraculis inter gentes patratis, quibus omnibus beneplacitum Dei de libertate a lege ceremoniali, & communione gentium absque circumcisione cum Israele in ea. Apostoli Petrus & Paulus supra clarissime demonstrarunt. Haec omnia Jacobus obsignat authoritate verbi Dei, quo libertatem illam praeindigitatam a Prophetis convincit. Suo nos exemplo docens, quanti Deum per Mosen & Prophetas loquentem & promittentem, & viam salutis monstrantem pendere debeamus. SICUT SCRIPTUM EST) Ex multis oraculis unicum citat, quod extat apud Amosum cap IX. v. 11. 12. Verba Amosi:
units.tr: Verse 15. AND TO THIS THE WORDS OF THE PROPHETS AGREE) He appeals to the time of promise, of prophecy, of vision and of expectation. It is the custom of the Apostles to refer the truth of their sayings back to Moses and the Prophets. And so that we may learn to value the authority and power of the Word of God, James sets it forth by the manifest testimonies of God: the Spirit of God given to the Gentiles, the purification of the heart, faith, the grace of Jesus Christ, and the signs and miracles wrought among the Gentiles. By all of these the good pleasure of God is shown, concerning liberty from the ceremonial law and the fellowship of the Gentiles with Israel in it without circumcision. The Apostles Peter and Paul demonstrated this most clearly above. James seals all these things with the authority of the Word of God, by which he proves that liberty, foretold beforehand by the Prophets. He teaches us by his own example how highly we ought to esteem God speaking and promising through Moses and the Prophets, and showing the way of salvation. AS IT IS WRITTEN) Out of many oracles he cites only one, which stands in Amos ch. 9, vv. 11, 12. The words of Amos:

units.la: Hoc est: Die illa excitabo tabernaculum Davidis collapsum, & sepe circumdabo ruptura ejus, demolitionesque ejus instaurabo, readificabóque eam ut retro temporibus, ut possideant reliquias Edom, & omnes alias gentes, quae nomine meo vocantur, dicit Dominus, faciens istud. Argumentum Jacobi: Tabernaculum Davidis in Christo restauran-dum, ejusdemque beneficio Ecclesiam Israeliticam gentes haereditaturam: Ergo gentes sine jugo legali ad communionem Christi pertinere. Excutiemus singula.
units.tr: That is: "On that day I will raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, and close up its breaches, and I will restore its ruins and rebuild it as in the days of old, that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the other nations which are called by my name, says the Lord who does this." The argument of James: the tabernacle of David is to be restored in Christ, and by his benefit the Israelite Church will inherit the Gentiles. Therefore the Gentiles, without the yoke of the law, belong to the fellowship of Christ. We shall examine each point.

units.la: Versus XVI. POSTHAEC) Denuntiavit vates Judaeis singulare Domini judicium in Republicae Israeliticae delectione, & statu populi eam consequente, a versu nono capitis octavi ad sextum noni. Defendit aequitatem judicii Dei, a versu sexto usque ad undecimum.
units.tr: Verse 16. AFTERWARDS) The prophet announced to the Jews the singular judgement of the Lord concerning the rejection of the Israelite commonwealth and the state of the people that follows from it, from verse 9 of chapter 8 to verse 6 of chapter 9. He defends the justice of God's judgement from verse 6 to verse 11.

units.la: cinum. Posthæc, quid facturus sit Dominus, edisserit. Hebraeus textus: בִיּוֹם הַהוּא In die illo. Intelligenda sunt de tempore Messiæ, quo Ecclesia Christi omnino instaurabitur. Abarbanel: בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן דֵּל הַקָּצוֹב לְפָנַי וְהַמְּגֻבָּל אֲצַלִי לִגְאֻלָּה In tempore illo, hoc est, definito coram me & determinato apud me ad redemptionem. Sic tergivetsatur Judaeus, ne determinatum temporis articulum cogatur in Messia figere, aut signa temporis agnoscere, quibus spes & consolatio fulciatur. Deinde addit: aut eo tempore, quo consumentur peccatores, & jactabuntur atque exagitabuntur. Contendit his verbis, Christum demum venturum post peractam illam Judaeorum exagitationem. Quam detorsionem, ex συναφεία praecedentium, octo rationibus confutavit Doctor Coccejus in Dodecaproph. p. 234.
units.tr: ...Afterwards, he sets out what the Lord will do. Hebrew text: [בַיּוֹם הַהוּא] "In that day." These words must be understood of the time of the Messiah, when the Church of Christ will be wholly restored. Abarbanel: [בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן דֵּל הַקָּצוֹב לְפָנַי וְהַמְּגֻבָּל אֲצַלִי לִגְאֻלָּה] "In that time, that is, the time fixed before me and determined by me for redemption." So the Jew equivocates, so that he will not be forced to fix the determined point of time in the Messiah, or to recognise the signs of the time by which hope and consolation are supported. Then he adds: "or at that time, when the sinners will be consumed and cast out and driven about." By these words he contends that Christ will come only after that persecution of the Jews has been completed. Doctor Cocceius, in his Dodecapropheton, p. 234, refuted this distortion with eight arguments drawn from the connection with what precedes.

units.la: REVERTAR) Non est in Hebraico textu: sed sensu convenit.
units.tr: I WILL RETURN) This is not in the Hebrew text, but it agrees in sense.

units.la: Praedixit enim deletionem Reipublicae Israeliticae, postquam cessante ira & justo judicio, Deus ad pristinum ingenium & bonitatem reditsurus. Sic egregie docet, cum antecedentibus connectenda, quae recitaturus ex Amoso.
units.tr: For he foretold the destruction of the Israelite commonwealth, after which, once anger has ceased and judgement has been carried out, God will return to his former disposition and goodness. Thus he rightly teaches that what he is about to recite from Amos is to be connected with what goes before.

units.la: ET RURSUS ÆDIFICABO TABERNACULUM DAVID) סכת דויד σκηνὴν Δαβίδ. סכה ad verbum idem est, quod opertorium, velamentum, tegumentum, tectum.
units.tr: AND I WILL BUILD AGAIN THE TABERNACLE OF DAVID) [סכת דויד] the tabernacle of David [σκηνὴν Δαβίδ]. Sukkah [סכה] means, word for word, the same as a covering, a veil, a shelter or a roof.

units.la: Promiserat Davidi Deus domum 2. Sam. VII. 11. כי בית יעשה לך יהוה Domum tibi faciet Deus. Hanc domum ipse David interpretatur, non pertinere ad semen sive domum suam carnalem, quippe אל כן non rectam coram Deo; sed ad ברית עולם foedus aeternum, fixum sibi, expositum inter omnes, & servatum de salute Davidis & Δόξα. Quae igitur 2. Sam. VII. dicta de domo Davidis, non κυρίως de Salomone intelligi, sed de Christo, ad quem etiam applicat Paulus Hebr. 1. 5. Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ εἰς πατέρα, καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι εἰς υἱόν. Hic est semen illud Davidis. Tugurium autem vel tabernaculum Davidis vocatur Christus, quia refugium praebet populo, qui in illo salvatur, & justitiam ac vitam per ipsum possidet. Pertinet huc Propheria Jeremiae cap. XXXIII. 15. 16. Diebus illis & tempore illo germinabit Davidi germen justitiae, & faciet judicium & justitiam in Terra. In diebus illis salvabitur Jehuda & Jerusalem: HABITABUNT securè, & hoc est nomen, quo vocabitur: Jehova justitia nostra. Ex quibus omnibus liquet, aedificationem domus Davidis esse darionem Messiae. Huic enim Deus promisit thronum Davidis Patris sui, in quo regnaret super domum Jacob in æternum, Luc. cap.I. 32.33. Errant igitur notoriè Ruffinus & Chrysostomus homil.33. in Acta, qui tabernaculi Davidis reædificationem factam censent ab Esdra & Zorobabel, qui Cyro annuente Judæos à Babylone reduxerunt in Jerusalem, ibíque postliminio Rempublicam & Ecclesiam Israeliticam restituerunt. Quam sententiam cùm tueretur Theodorus Mopsvestenus, à Vigilio Papa anathemate lancinatus est; rigidiùs equidem quàm par erat, in errore, in quo cardo Religionis non volvebatur.
units.tr: God had promised David a house (2 Sam. 7:11): "The LORD will make you a house" [כי בית יעשה לך יהוה]. David himself explains that this house does not refer to his carnal seed or house, which is "not right before God" [אל כן], but to "an everlasting covenant" [ברית עולם], fixed for him, set out before all, and kept, concerning the salvation of David and "glory" [Δόξα]. So what 2 Samuel 7 says of David's house is to be understood not strictly of Solomon but of Christ, to whom Paul also applies it (Heb. 1:5): "I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son" [Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι αὐτῷ εἰς πατέρα, καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται μοι εἰς υἱόν]. This is that seed of David. Christ is also called the tabernacle or hut of David, because he offers a refuge to the people who are saved in him and possess righteousness and life through him. To this belongs the prophecy of Jeremiah 33:15-16: "In those days and at that time I will raise up for David a branch of righteousness, and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land. In those days Judah shall be saved and Jerusalem shall dwell safely, and this is the name by which she shall be called: The LORD our righteousness." From all these things it is plain that the building up of David's house is the gift of the Messiah. For God promised him the throne of David his father, on which he would reign over the house of Jacob for ever (Luke 1:32-33). Therefore Rufinus and Chrysostom, in homily 33 on the Acts, are plainly wrong when they think the rebuilding of David's tabernacle was accomplished by Ezra and Zerubbabel, who, with Cyrus's consent, led the Jews back from Babylon to Jerusalem and there restored the Israelite state and Church after the exile. When Theodore of Mopsuestia defended this opinion, Pope Vigilius struck him with an anathema, more harshly, I admit, than was right, but in an error on which the hinge of religion did not turn.

units.la: QUOD COLLAPSUM EST) Prophetia est, ante Regnum Messiæ fore ruinam Regni posterorum Davidis.
units.tr: WHICH HAS FALLEN) It is a prophecy that, before the kingdom of the Messiah, there will be a ruin of the kingdom of David's descendants.

units.la: Clarè hoc David præindicavit in emortuali suo sermone 2.Sam. cap.XXIII.5. כל חפץ כי לא יצמיח Omne beneplacitum meum, si non germinabit, hoc est, si non erit שבט in Jehuda & מחקק sive Legislator in pedibus ejus, Gen.XLIX 10. Non est nostri instituti hoc loco in gradus & articulos hujus lapsûs & varias ruptuʀas inquirere, cùm ad quæstionis, quam Divus Jacobus tractat, momentum parum inde accedat.
units.tr: David clearly foretold this in his last words (2 Sam. 23:5): "Although my house is not so with God... for all my desire, if he will not make it grow" [כל חפץ כי לא יצמיח]; that is, if there will not be a sceptre [שבט] in Judah and a lawgiver [מחקק] between his feet (Gen. 49:10). It is not my purpose here to inquire into the stages and particulars of this fall or into its various breaches, since they contribute little to the question which the divine James is treating.

units.la: ET DIRUTA EJUS INSTAURABO) τὰ καταπεπτωκότα ἀνοικοδομήσω גדרתי את פרצין Pagninus Sepiam. Vatablus, instaurabo. Tigurina versio: Sepe circumdabo. Καταπαμμένα vocat Divus Jacobus, quod Amosus פרציהן ruptuʀas earum, subintellige Israelis & Judæ, vel duodecim tribuum, quæ resarciendæ & obsepiendæ cum adventu Christi, quomodo ἀπεκδέχεται illius adventum expectavit, & ad illius revelationem anhelavit, Act.XXVI 7. Descendit à καταπαύειν, quod est suffossione demoliri. ET ERIGAM ILLUD) Amosus: והקמתיו אקים & destructa ejus suscitabo. Respicit Prophetia ad resuscitationem corporis Christi. Quid enim aliud הרסות דוד destructa Davidis, quàm corpus Christi, qui ut Filius Davidis, ita etiam David vocatur. Illud erectum est per Spiritum ἀγιωσύνης, Rom.I.4. Juxta resuscitationem destructi corporis Christi, secundum analogiam mysterii Fidei, historiæ & Prophetiæ intelligi potest dispersio discipulorum Christi, & eorum recreatio & recollectio. Versus XVII. UT REQUIRANT QUI RELIQUI SUNT HOMINES DOMINUM) ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ καταλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν κύριον. Amosus sic: למען ירשו את שארית אדום וכל הגוים Ut hæreditent reliquias Edom, & omnes alias Gentes. sic. te. Notabilis, ut apparet, Jacobum Apostolum inter & Amosum, differentia, quod verba concernit. Nam pro hæreditare Lucas habet requirere: pro Edom/ homines, & addit τὸν κύριον. Ex Septuaginta interpretibus Amosi sententiam à Luca citatam, nequit ambigi, quorum versio sic habet: Ὅπως ἐκζητήσωσι με οἱ καταλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων. Sed & fons erroris apertus est. Septuaginta enim pro יִרְשׁוּ legerunt יִרְשׁוּ pro אֱרוֹם appellativum אָדָם Quid ergo? Annon ejusmodi exemplis Septuaginta Viralis supra Hebræum Codicem nobilitatur? Absit multum, multumque absit, quicquid pro authoritate ejus Divina Johannes Morinus, antiquorum nonnullorum hyperbolas secutus & alii contendant. Nam Apostoli honorem habuerunt celeberrimæ & usitatissimæ inter Judæos Hellenistas versioni, quandiu citra jacturam fidei adeóque salvâ dictorum Propheticorum substantiâ licuit, ut & libertatem suam testarentur, & in re levi malis cavillorum, infirmis scandali occasionem nullam præberent. Si constaret, in capitali dissensu Hebraici Codicis & Græcæ versionis, Apostolos huic potiùs quàm illi acquievisse, profectò insignis hæc prærogativæ indicina foret. Sed nihil tale unquam fecerunt. Certè in præsenti textu nihil Jacobus ex Græco citavit, quod non τὴν Ἀλγόναν in Hebraico textu sit comprehensum, quin egregia ejus paraphrasi illustratum. Hæc συμφωνία liquidò apparebit, ubi & Amosi & Jacobi verba explicatiora dederimus. Ergo vaticinatur Amosus, Ecclesiam, in qua regnum suum Christus fundavit, hæreditaturam reliquias Edomi & Gentes, super quas invocatum nomen Domini. Nempe Abrahami filiis promissa est hæreditas mundi, non omnibus tamen, quia multi peccatores fuerunt, sed reliquiis, Esaj. X.21.22. Ubi Propheta vaticinatur, fore illo tempore, ut non pergat ultra שְׁאָר יִשְׂרָאֵל reliquum Israelis & פְּלֵיטַת qui evadet ex Jacob, adhærere suo percussori, sed innitatur Jehovæ Sancto Israelis fideliter. Ergo his Deus promisit hæreditatem gentium, Genes. XV.6. XVII.2.3. &c. Apostolus vocat κληρονομίαν τοῦ κόσμου, Rom.IV.13. Ejus hæc natura est, ut Abraham sit אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם Pater multitudinis Gentium, Genes.XVII.2. πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν Rom.IV.17. & ut omnes filii terræ fiant filii Abrahami, hoc est, qui στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσι τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως τοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ qui insistunt vestigiis fidei Abrahami Patris Rom IV.12. Ut sic omnes, qui sunt ex fide, accipiant benedictionem cum fideli Abrahamo. hamo, Gal.III.9. Quæ benedictio cum Abrahamo nihil aliud est quàm justificatio & non imputatio peccati, v.8. Hoc fit, cùm obediunt Christo, & recipiunt Evangelium regni per fidem. Jamin eo semine primæ tribuuntur Edomo, ante reliquas Gentes. Quæ ratio? Respicit Propheta ad tempora Davidis, qui Idumeam illustri victoria subjugavit, 2.Sam.VIII.13.14. Psal.LX.10.11. [Hebrew] In Idumeam extendam calceamentum meum. Pollicetur David sibi possessionem Idumeæ immissione calceamenti, quæ fuit olim forma introducendi in possessionem. Sicut igitur victoriam carnalem tulit de Idumæis Rex David, sic Christus per Apostolos, adeóque Ecclesia Novi Testamenti immissione calceamenti subjugabit sibi Idumæam, & illam hæreditabit. Deinde notat Spiritus Sanctus hæreditare hac Edomi, sublatis inimicitiis pacem Ecclesiæ cessuram. Nam sicut Esavus internecino odio persecutus est Jacobum, sic posteri Esavi Idumæi Israëlitas, quibus infensissimi fuerunt. His igitur conciliatis supererat, ut reliquæ gentes minori negotio hæreditarentur, & sic intraret plenitudo earum. Neque tamen in universum omnium Idumæorum hæreditatem Ecclesia cernere debuit. Hinc Amosus vocat [Hebrew] reliquias, nempe [Hebrew] qui evaderet ex manu percussoris, & niteretur Jehova Sancto Israëlis. Rursum habemus hujus rei præcedentem typum, quando David per Joabum cæsis plerisque Idumæis servavit tantùm reliquias, 1.Reg.XI.14. Sic paulò ante tempora Amosi Amazias Rex Jehudæ percussit Edom, in urbe Sela servavit & subjugavit, 2.Reg. cap. XIV.7. Denique sicut non omnes Israëlitæ sunt ad Christum conversi, adeóque hæreditati Christi cesserunt, sed [Hebrew] tantùm, id est, reliquiæ, sic etiam Deus servavit per præconium Evangelii non omnes Edomitas, & reliquarum gentium homines, sed reliquias tantùm, nempe eos, qui prædicationi Evangelii crediderunt, cæteris ob infidelitatem pereuntibus. Sic tenemus mentem Prophetæ: Ventura nempe tempora, quibus Ecclesia sub Regno Messiæ, non conclusa amplius Israëlitice possessionis angustiis, hæreditatem adeat etiam Edomitarum, imò omnium gentium, non tamen omnium in gentibus hominum, sed reliquiarum earum, id est, eorum, qui refugium quærunt in Sancto Israëlis, & eo niituntur, & eum requirunt, per quem extra metum percussoris tuti collocantur. Quid hic diversum à Jacobo Apostolo dictum in Concilio, si sensum ejus spectes? Ut requirant reliqui homines Dominum, & omnes gentes. Certè Edom & gentes non possunt esse hæreditas Israëlis sub Christo, nisi quatenus & quando incipiunt requirere Dominum. Ergo pro Edomitis Jacobus posuit requirentes Dominum, pro specie genus, pro exemplo quosvis alios exemplum imitantes. Deinde, quia Amos per ΓΝΥ intellexit Edomi reliquias, id est, credentes, quia hos jam expressit sub nomine quærentium Dominum, ideo per κα-ταλοιπος των ανθρωπων in contradistinctione cæterarum gentium, intelligit homines Palæstinæ vicinos, & ab Israële discretos, inter quos ipsi etiam Idumæi fuerunt. Sic videmus Amosum & Jacobum sibi amicè concordes, operas mutuas tradere,
units.tr: AND I WILL REPAIR ITS BREACHES) τὰ καταπεπτωκότα ἀνοικοδομήσω [גדרתי את פרצין]. Pagninus translates "I will hedge"; Vatablus, "I will repair"; the Tigurine version, "I will surround with a hedge." James calls them "the things fallen down" [καταπεπτωκότα], where Amos has "their breaches" [פרציהן], that is, of Israel and Judah, or of the twelve tribes, which were to be repaired and fenced in at the coming of Christ, just as James, awaiting his coming, "looked for" it [ἀπεκδέχεται] and longed for its revelation (Acts 26:7). The word derives from katapauein, meaning to pull down by digging underneath. AND I WILL RAISE IT UP) Amos has "and I will raise up its ruins" [והקמתיו אקים], "its destroyed parts." The prophecy looks to the raising of the body of Christ. For what else is "the ruined dwelling of David" [הרסות דוד] than the body of Christ, who is called the Son of David and also David? That body was raised up "by the Spirit of holiness" (Rom. 1:4). By analogy with the resurrection of the destroyed body of Christ, and according to the analogy of the mystery of faith, of history and of prophecy, one can understand the scattering of Christ's disciples and their restoration and gathering again. VERSE 17, THAT THE REST OF MANKIND MAY SEEK THE LORD) ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ καταλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν κύριον. Amos has: "that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations" [למען ירשו את שארית אדום וכל הגוים], and so on. There is, as is evident, a notable difference between the Apostle James and Amos in wording. For "to possess" [hæreditare] Luke has "to seek" [requirere]; for "Edom" he has "men," and he adds "the Lord" [τὸν κύριον]. That the sense of Amos quoted by Luke is taken from the Septuagint cannot be doubted, whose version reads: "That the rest of men may seek me" [Ὅπως ἐκζητήσωσι με οἱ καταλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων]. The source of the error is also obvious: the Septuagint read [יִרְשׁוּ] for [יִרְשׁוּ] and, for the proper name [אֱרוֹם] Edom, the common noun [אָדָם] man. What then? Does the Septuagint, through examples of this kind, not gain esteem above the Hebrew codex? Far be it, very far be it, from us to hold anything of this sort for its divine authority, as Johannes Morinus and some others contend, following the hyperboles of certain ancient writers. For the Apostles held in honour the most celebrated and most commonly used version among the Hellenistic Jews, so long as this could be done without loss of faith and so without harm to the substance of the prophetic words, both to bear witness to their own liberty and to give the malicious quibblers and the weak no occasion of offence. If it were established that, in a fundamental disagreement between the Hebrew codex and the Greek version, the Apostles had acquiesced in the latter rather than the former, this would indeed be a striking proof of such a privilege. But they never did anything of the kind. Certainly in the present text James cited nothing from the Greek that is not contained in the Hebrew text, and it is illuminated by his excellent paraphrase. This agreement will become quite clear when we have given fuller explanations of the words of Amos and of James. Therefore Amos prophesies that the Church, in which Christ founded his kingdom, will possess the remnant of Edom and the nations over whom the name of the Lord has been called. Indeed the inheritance of the world was promised to the sons of Abraham, but not to all of them, because many were sinners, only to a remnant (Isa. 10:21-22). There the prophet foretells that at that time the remnant of Israel and the survivor of Jacob will no longer lean on the one who struck them, but will faithfully rest on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel. So God promised the inheritance of the nations to Abraham (Gen. 15:6; 17:2-3, etc.). The Apostle calls it "the inheritance of the world" (Rom. 4:13). Its nature is that Abraham should be [אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם] "a father of a multitude of nations" (Gen. 17:2), [πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν] (Rom. 4:17), and that all the sons of the earth should become sons of Abraham, that is, those who [στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσι τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως τοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ] "walk in the footsteps of the faith of our father Abraham" in uncircumcision (Rom. 4:12), so that all who are of faith may receive the blessing with faithful Abraham (Gal. 3:9). This blessing with Abraham is nothing other than justification and the non-imputation of sin (v. 8). This happens when they obey Christ and receive the gospel of the kingdom through faith. Now in this seed the first place is given to Edom before the rest of the nations. Why? The prophet looks back to the time of David, who subdued Idumea by a famous victory (2 Sam. 8:13-14; Ps. 60:10-11), [בְּאֱדוֹם אַשְׁלִיךְ נַעֲלִי] "Over Edom will I cast my shoe." David promises himself possession of Idumea by the casting of a shoe, which was once the form of putting someone into possession. Therefore, just as King David won a carnal victory over the Idumeans, so Christ through the Apostles, and thus the Church of the New Testament, by casting the shoe will subdue Idumea to himself and make it his inheritance. Next the Holy Spirit signifies that the inheritance of Edom, once enmities are removed, will yield peace to the Church. For just as Esau persecuted Jacob with deadly hatred, so the descendants of Esau, the Idumeans, were most hostile to the Israelites. With these reconciled, it remained that the other nations should be inherited with less difficulty, and so the fullness of them would enter. Yet the Church was not obliged to look for the inheritance of all the Idumeans as a whole. Hence Amos calls them [שְׁאָרִית] "remnants," namely [פְּלֵיטַת] those who escape from the hand of the one who strikes, and who lean upon the LORD, the Holy One of Israel. Again we have a preceding type of this matter, when David through Joab, after most of the Idumeans had been slain, spared only the remnants (1 Kings 11:14-16). So shortly before the time of Amos, King Amaziah of Judah struck Edom, and spared and subdued it in the city of Sela (2 Kings 14:7). Finally, just as not all Israelites were converted to Christ, and so did not yield to Christ's inheritance, but only [שְׁאָרִית], that is, a remnant, so God through the proclamation of the gospel has spared not all the Edomites and the men of the other nations, but only a remnant, namely those who believed the preaching of the gospel, while the rest perished through unbelief. Thus we grasp the mind of the prophet: that the coming times, when the Church under the kingdom of the Messiah, no longer shut up within the narrow limits of Israelite possession, will enter upon the inheritance of the Edomites and indeed of all the nations, not indeed of all the men among the nations, but of a remnant of them, that is, of those who seek refuge in the Holy One of Israel, lean upon him, and seek him, through whom they are placed in safety beyond the fear of the one who strikes. What, if you look at the sense, is different from what the Apostle James said in the council? "That the rest of men may seek the Lord, and all the nations." Certainly Edom and the nations cannot be the inheritance of Israel under Christ except insofar as and when they begin to seek the Lord. So James, in place of the Edomites, put "those who seek the Lord," the genus for the species, and for an example any others who imitate the example. Then, because Amos understood by the remnant [שְׁאָרִית] of Edom, that is, believers, and because he had already expressed these under the name of those who seek the Lord, therefore by "the rest of men" [καταλοιπος των ανθρωπων], in contrast with the other nations, he means the men of Palestine who were neighbours of Israel and distinct from it, among whom the Idumeans themselves were included. Thus we see Amos and James agreeing in friendship with each other, lending each other mutual help.

units.la: SUPER QUAS INVOCATUM EST NOMEN MEUM)
units.tr: WHICH MY NAME IS CALLED UPON

units.la: In his verbis modus communionis reliquiarum Edomi & Gentium cum reliquiis Israelis consistit, & nervus argumenti Jacobi. Invocatur nomen Domini supra eum, qui est populus Dei, cœtus & Ecclesia Christi, qui habet nomen Domini, tanquam rem sibi propriam. Confer similia phraseos exempla Jes.IV.1.XLIII.6. LIII.11. Joel.III.5. Hinc etiam Apostolus concludit Rom.X.13. salvatum iri gentes, quia επικαλεσονται το ονομα Κυριου, nomen Domini super ipsos invocatur. Concludit igitur ex præsenti Amos Prophetia το κεκλημενον, nempe Deum decrevisse justificare & salvare gentes per fidem, absque onere legis. Fundamentum hujus conclusionis est, quòd hic unicum medium communionis exprimitur, Nuncupari à nomine Domini, hoc est, se Christo addicere ad populum, ad peculium, & gloriari in beneficio redemptionis ejus. Nihil autem de onere legis, cujus conditionem omnino Deus præfixisset, si esset vinculum communionis gentium cum Judæis. Nam antehac rigidissimè recepta hæc ceremonialia sunt, Proselythis ad Ecclesiam Israeliticam injuncta. Cùm igitur in hæreditatem cesserint illi μα-θηται, reliquiæ Edomi & gentium Ecclesiæ Israeliticæ sine expressa conditione chirographi, acquiescendum esse consilio & decreto Dei, neque jugum hoc ipsis imponendum.
units.tr: In these words the manner of fellowship between the remnant of Edom and the Gentiles with the remnant of Israel rests, and this is the strength of James's argument. The name of the Lord is called upon over him who is the people of God, the assembly and Church of Christ, who has the name of the Lord as his own possession. Compare similar examples of this phrase at Isa. 4.1; 43.6; 53.11; Joel 3.5. Hence the Apostle also concludes at Rom. 10.13 that the Gentiles will be saved, because they shall call upon the name of the Lord [ἐπικαλέσονται τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου]. So from the present prophecy of Amos he concludes that those who are called [τὸ κεκλημένον], that is, the Gentiles, God has decreed to justify and save through faith, without the burden of the law. The foundation of this conclusion is that the only means of fellowship expressed here is to be named by the name of the Lord, that is, to devote oneself to Christ, to the people and to his own possession, and to glory in the benefit of his redemption. Nothing is said about the burden of the law, whose condition God would have expressly laid down if it were to be the bond of fellowship between the Gentiles and the Jews. For these ceremonial matters were until then most strictly required of proselytes joining the Israelite Church. Since therefore those disciples [μαθηταί], the remnant of Edom and the Gentiles, have come into the inheritance of the Israelite Church without the express condition of the bond, we must acquiesce in the counsel and decree of God, and this yoke must not be laid upon them.

units.la: DICIT DOMINUS)
units.tr: SAITH THE LORD

units.la: Jehova, qui per hoc beneficium fit id quod est, & verum se Jehovam, constantem in suis promissis, & eventu illa repræsentantem præstat & demonstrat. Unde patet, conversionem & fidem Gentium esse non rem inefficacis desiderii aut propensionis, sed firmi propositi, & verbo declarati, & fidelibus ad credendum publicati, adeoque per fidem & spem sanctorum ratifi-cati, & in vim fœderis ac contractus traducti.
units.tr: Jehovah, who by this benefit makes himself what he is, and shows and proves himself to be the true Jehovah, constant in his promises and making them present in their outcome. From this it is plain that the conversion and faith of the Gentiles is not a matter of an ineffective wish or inclination, but of a firm purpose, declared in the Word and published to believers for belief, and so ratified through the faith and hope of the saints, and brought into the force of a covenant and contract.

units.la: QUI FACIT HOC) Hoc firmamentum est promissionis Divinæ. Nempe quia fundatio Regni Christi, & ejus per hæreditatem Edomi & gentium amplificatio, non est opus hominis, sed Dei, ideo nemo ei resistere debet, quò minùs adoptentur in Ecclesiam, & reliquiæ Israelis hæreditatem suam adeant.
units.tr: WHO DOES THIS) This is the firm foundation of the divine promise. Namely, because the founding of Christ's kingdom, and its enlargement through the inheritance of Edom and the Gentiles, is not the work of man but of God, therefore no one ought to resist him, so that they are not admitted into the Church and the remnant of Israel does not enter upon its inheritance.

units.la: Versus XVIII. NOTA à SECULO DEO OMNIA OPERA EJUS)
units.tr: Verse 18. KNOWN TO GOD FROM THE AGE ALL HIS WORKS

units.la: Complutensis editio legit ἀ ἐχ γνωστὰ ἀπ' αἰῶνος αὐτῷ. Quæ sunt ipsi nota à Seculo. Vetus Interpres: Notum à Domino à Seculo est opus suum. Nempe in antiquis quibusdam Codicibus habetur γνωστὸν παῦ το ἔργον. Syrus in plurali ידיעין אנין מן עלמא עבורה דאלהא Nota sunt ab æterno opera Deo. Mens Jacobi hæc est, debere Deo credi in prædictionibus & promissionibus suis, quia omnia sua opera ante Deus decrevit, & nihil decrevit, quod non in tempore faciat. Deinde, ex opere Dei sensum promissionis esse æstimandum; si quid generalius vel indefinitius videatur Deus prædixisse, aut per ænigma, rudibus non statim pervium. Ita opus Dei erat baptismus Cornelii per Spiritum S. accommodatum verbis Amos, quibus declaratur, Gentes denominatas à nomine Dei, fore hæreditatem, & habituras communionem cum Israele. Ex quo sequebatur, mentem illius prophetiæ esse, ut gentes incircumcisæ habeant partem in sanctificatione & justificatione. Cæterùm universale hoc axioma probat, Deum omniscium ab æterno scientia suâ complexum omnia, quæ in tempore facit opera, atque adeò etiam ea, quæ à libera voluntate pendent, quippe quæ in tempore facit. Ex qua præscientia fluit, quòd in tempore nulla creatura aliter facere potest, quàm facit. Et prodigiosus est in eo non error, sed furor Fausti Socini, qui in dubium vocare sustinuit tam claris documentis testatam in Deo præsciam futurorum mentem. Quò audaciæ vix quisquam Gentilium unquam processit. Sed sic præcordia excutere, & ultima experiri homo debuit, ut omnia Dei decreta & ejus circa salutem nostram operatio & dominium excluderetur, & homo per liberi arbitrii vires in jus independentiæ asserere-tur. Hic ulcus, & manus quæ fricat! Operæ pretium est audire Socinum, præsentem textum eludentem. Tres sunt, inquit Præleg. cap.9. hujus loci lectiones. Prima Veteris Interpretis: Notum à Domino mino
units.tr: The Complutensian edition reads ἀ ἐχ γνωστὰ ἀπ' αἰῶνος αὐτῷ [things known to him from of old]. Things that are known to him from the age. The Old Interpreter: Known to the Lord from the age is his work. Indeed in some old manuscripts there is γνωστὸν ... τὸ ἔργον [known ... the work]. The Syriac has in the plural yedi'in anin min 'alma 'ubada d'Alaha [the works of God are known from eternity]. The meaning of James is this: God must be believed in his predictions and promises, because he decreed all his works before, and decreed nothing that he does not do in time. Next, from the work of God the sense of a promise is to be judged: if God seems to have foretold something more general or indefinite, or in an enigma not at once plain to the simple, then the work of God is to be understood. Thus the baptism of Cornelius by the Holy Spirit was the work of God, fitted to the words of Amos, by which it is declared that the Gentiles named by the name of God would become an inheritance and would have fellowship with Israel. From this it followed that the meaning of that prophecy is that the uncircumcised Gentiles should have a share in sanctification and justification. Moreover, this universal axiom proves that God, who knows all things, from eternity embraced by his knowledge all the works he performs in time, and therefore also those which depend on free will, since he performs them in time. From this foreknowledge it follows that in time no creature can act otherwise than it does. And in this it is a monstrous thing, not an error but a frenzy, in Faustus Socinus, who ventured to call into doubt the mind of God, foreknowing future things, so clearly attested by plain documents. To such audacity hardly any of the Gentiles ever went. But a man had to shake his inmost heart in this way and test his last resources, so that all God's decrees, and his working and dominion over our salvation, might be shut out, and man be asserted, by the powers of free choice, into a right of independence. Here is the sore, and the hand that rubs it! It is worth hearing Socinus, who evades the present text. There are three, he says in the Prolegomena, chapter 9, readings of this place. The first, of the Old Interpreter: "Known to the Lord

units.la: cap.9. hujus loci lectiones. mino à seculo est opus suum. Quæ verba nihil aliud significant, quàm Deum opus illud, de quo ibi sermo erat, ab ipso avo cognovisse, id est, facere decrevisse. Si facere decrevit, ergo præscivit. Nisi forte decerni potest non cognitum. Quicquid sit, inquit, id tantum colligi potest, Deum vocationem gentium præcognitam habuisse à seculo. Sed quid ex prænotione ista sui operis ad prænotionem humanorum factorum stabiliendam colligi potest? Respondeo. Dato, non intelligi quidquam aliud, quàm prænotionem vocationis Gentium. Præcognovit sanè eodem modo obedientiam Gentium, quo earum vocationem. Aliàs fieri potuisset, ut inanis esset Evangelii sonus, & reliquiæ Edomi & gentium non hæreditarentur. Imò opus Dei, quod prænovit, est etiam τὸ ἐπιζητῆν τὸν κύριον, v.17. quæ ipsa est obedientia Evangelica. Obedientia autem ex hypothesi Socini fuit libera. Ergo prænovit Deus vocationem Gentium, & obedientiam eorum liberam, adeóque aliquod contingens futurum. Qui novit unicum futurum contingentem effectum, is habet mentem præsciam futurorum. Cur ergo cætera non prænosceret, cùm infinita scientia futura comprehendens requiratur æquè ad unum scibile contingens, atque ad infinita? Pergit: In Complutensi similiter editione simpliciter scriptum est: ὰ ἐκ γνωσὰ ἀπ' αἰῶνος αὐτῷ. Quæ sunt ipsi nota à Seculo. Unde nihil colligi potest, nisi ea, de quibus ibi verba fiebant, nota fuisse Deo ab æterno. Ea opera ipsum Dei esse, inter omnes constat. Huic effugio jam occurrimus. Restat, inquit, vulgata Graecorum Codicum lectio, quæ Latinè ita sonat: Nota à seculo sunt Deo omnia opera sua. Ex quibus verbis tantum abest, ut colligi possit, omnia prorsus Deo nota esse, antequam fiant, ut potius contrarium colligi posse videatur, nempe quædam esse ex iis, quæ nondum sunt, quæ Deo à seculo non sint cognita. Mirum si ex tam clara luce tenebras creare potest. Quid enim, inquit, attinebat operum Dei nominatim mentionem facere, si nihil plané esset, quod à seculo Deo cognitum non fuisset? Ergo non omne quod fit, est opus Dei. Non igitur Deus omnia fecit propter se ipsum, etiam malum ad diem mali, Prov. XVI.4. Non in Deo sumus, vivimus & movemur, Act. XVII.28. Non ex ipso, & per ipsum & in ipsum sunt omnia, Rom. XI.36. Neq; unus Deus Pater, ex quo omnia, & nos in ipsum, 1. Cor. VIII.6. Apage impietatem! Hócine grato & pio nominis Christi confessore dignum, ubique manus & Spiritum Dei abbreviare, ut humanæ potentiæ peristromata dilates? Quanquam, pergit, Erasmus & Tigurini ita locum interpretantur, ut ad ea tantùm omnia Dei opera verbà Jacobi accommodentur, de quibus locutus fuerat. Articulum enim πρὸ pronominis loco accipiunt. Unde tanto magis suspicabimur, praenotionem Dei ex loco ipso non modò non confirmari, sed etiam everti, quippe ex quo colligi queat, quaedam tantummodo opera à seculo cognita fuisse. Cum Erasmo & Tigurinis invitis & obtorto collo raptis vindemiam facit. Illis nihil minùs in animo fuit, quàm praescientiam Dei sua interpretatione in discrimen adducere. Restringunt quidem πάντες ad subjectam materiam. Sed quis ferat Socinum ita disputantem: Erasmus & Tigurini illa πάντες, à Deo ab aeterno praecognita, restringunt ad praesentem materiam de vocatione Gentium: Ergo ex iis colligi potest, quaedam tantùm opera Deo à seculo cognita esse. An qui simpliciter dicit, quaedam opera Deo ab aeterno cognita esse, quorum in eo textu fit mentio, & quae maximè intererat ad Divinam praenotionem referri, caetera opera, quae evidenter Dei esse constat, à praescientia Dei excludit? Facessat dementia. Instat: Dei opus non illud omne proprie dici potest, quod Deus operatur, sed illud demum, quod ex sola voluntate ejus pendet, nec ad hominis actiones respectum habet, qualis gentium vocatio. Resp. Dei opus est, quod facit. Nihil autem non facit ipse. Etiam maximè contingentia & liberrima pendent à Deo operante. Non sumus idonei ex nobis ipsis tanquam ex nobis λογίζεσθαι, sed omnis nostra aptitudo est à Deo, 2. Cor. III. 5. Quin ipse est in nobis ὁ ἐνεργῶν καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν, Phil. II. 13. Deinde vocatio Gentium, quam sequitur actio hominis, quaerere Dominum, & ejus communionem appetere, non est tale opus, quod ad actiones hominis respectum nullum habeat. Et tamen, Socino fatente, fuit ab aeterno praecognita. Ergo praenosci potuit opus, cum quo voluntas hominis in tempore concurrit.
units.tr: from the age is his work." These words signify nothing other than that God knew from the grandfather that work of which the discussion there was, that is, that he decreed to do it. If he decreed to do it, then he foreknew it. Unless perhaps one can decree what is not known. Whatever it is, he says, this alone can be gathered, that God had the calling of the Gentiles foreknown from the age. But what can be gathered from that foreknowledge of his own work to establish the foreknowledge of human deeds? I answer. Granting that nothing else is understood than the foreknowledge of the calling of the Gentiles. He certainly foreknew the obedience of the Gentiles in the same way as their calling. Otherwise it could have come about that the sound of the Gospel was empty, and the remnant of Edom and the Gentiles did not inherit. Indeed the work of God which he foreknew is also τὸ ἐπιζητῆν τὸν κύριον [to seek the Lord], v. 17, which is itself evangelical obedience. But obedience, on the hypothesis of Socinus, was free. Therefore God foreknew the calling of the Gentiles, and their free obedience, and so some future contingent thing. He who knows a single future contingent effect has a mind that foreknows future things. Why then should he not foreknow the rest, since infinite knowledge comprehending the future is required equally for one contingent knowable thing as for infinite ones? He goes on: In the Complutensian edition likewise it is simply written: ἀ ἐχ γνωστὰ ἀπ' αἰῶνος αὐτῷ, "things known to him from the age." Whence nothing can be gathered except that those things of which the words there were speaking were known to God from eternity. That those works are God's own, is agreed by all. To this evasion we are already coming. There remains, he says, the common reading of the Greek codices, which in Latin sounds thus: "All his works are known to God from the age." From these words it is so far from being gathered that all things whatever were known to God before they came to be, that rather the contrary seems to be gathered, namely that some of those things which are not yet, are not known to God from the age. It is strange if he can make darkness out of such clear light. For what, he says, was the point of making mention by name of the works of God, if there were nothing at all which was not known to God from the age? Therefore not everything that happens is a work of God. Therefore God did not make all things for himself, even the evil for the day of evil, Prov. 16.4. We are not in God, we live and move, Acts 17.28. Not from him, through him and to him are all things, Rom. 11.36. Nor is there one God the Father, from whom all things, and we unto him, 1 Cor. 8.6. Away with impiety! Is it worthy of a grateful and pious confessor of the name of Christ to shorten the hand and Spirit of God everywhere, so as to widen the coverlets of human power? Although, he goes on, Erasmus and the Tigurines interpret the place thus, that the words of James apply to all those works of God only of which he had spoken. For they take the article πρό in place of a pronoun. Whence we shall suspect all the more that the foreknowledge of God is not only not confirmed from the place itself, but even overturned, since from it can be gathered that only some works were known from the age. With Erasmus and the Tigurines unwillingly and against their will he gathers the vintage. They had nothing less in mind than to bring God's foreknowledge into danger by their interpretation. They indeed restrict πάντες [all] to the subject matter. But who could bear Socinus disputing thus: Erasmus and the Tigurines restrict those "all" things, foreknown by God from eternity, to the present matter of the calling of the Gentiles: therefore from them it can be gathered that only some works were known to God from the age. Or does he who simply says that some works were known to God from eternity, of which mention is made in that text, and which it was most of all important to refer to the divine foreknowledge, exclude from the foreknowledge of God the other works which it is plain are evidently God's? Let such madness depart. He insists: The work of God cannot properly be called all that God works, but only that which depends solely on his will and has no regard to human actions, such as the calling of the Gentiles. I reply: the work of God is what he does. He does nothing that he does not himself do. Even the most contingent and most free things depend on God working. We are not sufficient of ourselves, as of ourselves λογίζεσθαι [to reckon anything], but all our fitness is from God, 2 Cor. 3.5. Indeed he himself is in us ὁ ἐνεργῶν καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν [who works both to will and to work], Phil. 2.13. Further, the calling of the Gentiles, which is followed by the action of man in seeking the Lord and desiring his fellowship, is not such a work as has no regard to human actions. And yet, Socinus admitting it, it was foreknown from eternity. Therefore a work with which the human will concurs in time could be foreknown.

units.la: Versus XIX. QUAPROPTER EGO CENSEO)
units.tr: Verse 19. WHEREFORE I JUDGE

units.la: Κρίνω. Judico. Haec igitur sententia Jacobi, quae sequitur, est judiciaria & definitiva. Est enim κρίσις judicium & decretum animi, gravibus rationibus definitum & conclusum, & ad fidem conscientiam obligans. Haec formula in Apostolos plane competebat, quippe quorum θεμέλιο sumus superaedificati, Ephes. II. 20. Quorum adeo vox & scripta sunt λειτουργίαι τῶν ἐπουρανίων, Hebr. cap. IV. vers. 12. In fidelibus autem quibuscunque κρίσις quidem requiritur spiritualium, lium, quatenus est certum animi decretum, non tamen alios ad fidem obligat, nisi quatenus illud convenit cum regula fidei & verbis fundamenti.
units.tr: Κρίνω. [Κρίνω] I judge. This sentence of James, which follows, is therefore judicial and definitive. For κρίσις [κρίσις] is a judgment and decision of the mind, settled and concluded on weighty grounds, and binding the conscience to belief. This form of words properly belonged to the Apostles, of whom we are "built upon the foundation" (Ephes. 2:20), and whose voice and writings are the λειτουργίαι τῶν ἐπουρανίων [ministries of heavenly things] (Heb. 4:12). In other believers, however, a κρίσις is indeed required of spiritual persons, insofar as it is a settled decision of the mind; yet it does not bind others to belief, except insofar as it agrees with the rule of faith and the words of the foundation.

units.la: NON OBTURBANDUM ESSE) Μὴ παρενοχλεῖν. Sic vertunt Pagninus, Stephanus, Erasmus, Tigurini, Beza. Hoc enim sonare videtur Praepositio עכר. Syrus מטל הדא אנא אמר אנא דלא נחזין Propterea ego hoc dico, ne obturbent eos. Vetat Jacobus, ne turbentur, nimia mole, qualis jugum illud, obruantur, & offendantur vel verbis vel factis teneriores conscientiae, ne Evangelii cursus praepostero sufflamine sistatur. ILLIS, QUI EX GENTIBUS CONVERTUNTUR AD DEUM) Quos supra nomine μαθητῶν insignivit.
units.tr: THAT THEY SHOULD NOT BE TROUBLED) Μὴ παρενοχλεῖν [Mē parenochlein]. Thus Pagninus, Stephanus, Erasmus, the Tigurines and Beza translate it. For the preposition עכר seems to carry this sense. The Syriac has (transliterated) "matel hada ana amar ana dela nachezin", i.e. Therefore I say this, lest they trouble them. James forbids that the more tender consciences be troubled and overwhelmed by a great burden, such as that yoke, and be offended either by words or deeds, lest the course of the Gospel be checked by a premature hindrance. TO THOSE FROM THE GENTILES WHO ARE CONVERTED TO GOD) Whom he has marked above with the name of disciples.

units.la: Versus XX. SED SCRIBENDUM AD EOS) Ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι. Particula ἀλλὰ est exceptiva pro εἰ μή. Quasi diceret: Nolo quidem, obrui discipulos mole legum ceremonialium, quales infinitae à Mose sunt praescriptae. Attamen excipio abstinentiam ab idolothytis &c. literis ipsis mandandam. Syrus אלא נשתלח למון Sed ut mittantur ad eos.
units.tr: Verse 20. BUT THAT THEY BE WRITTEN TO) Ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι [Alla episteilai]. The particle ἀλλὰ [alla] is exceptive, in place of εἰ μή [ei mē]. As if he were saying: I indeed do not wish the disciples to be crushed by the mass of ceremonial laws, of which Moses prescribed countless kinds. Yet I make an exception: abstinence from things offered to idols, etc., is to be enjoined in writing. The Syriac has (transliterated) "ela nishtalach lemon", i.e. But that they be sent to them.

units.la: UT ABSTINEANT SE AB INQUINAMENTIS SIMULACHRORUM, ET SCORTATIONE, ET SUFFOCATO, ET SANGUINE) Haec paulò diligentius trutinabimus in fine Concilii ad versum 29. Versus XXI. MOSES ENIM AB ANTIQUIS AETATIBUS IN SINGULIS CIVITATIBUS HABET, QUI IPSUM PRAEDICENT) Periodus occupationis rationem habet. Sed sensus ipse nonnihil involutus est. Cornelius à Lapide ita interpretatur, tanquam Jacobus his verbis Judaizantes traduceret, & res suas sibi habere juberet. Facit enim ita loquentem: Non est, quòd nos Christiani simus solliciti de Mose honorando. Moses enim & lex satis honorantur & celebrantur à Judaeis in suis Synagogis. Judaei ergo, qui Moisis honorem zelant, ejus Synagogas adeant, ibidemque ipsum celebrent. Nobis Christianis sufficit in Ecclesia Christum, ad quem Moses remisit Deut. XVIII. 18. ejúsque legem celebrare. Chrysostomo tribuit eandem sententiam Cornelius. Nescio quàm verè. Nam Chrysostomus vult, Jacobum reddere rationem, cur non esset necessum hac de re scribere ad Judaeos, qui fidem Christi amplexi erant, sicut ad Gentiles: nem-
